obtained.how: university repository: University of Manitoba MSpace, open PDF of the thesis (the handle in the entry, 1993/832; file mq23264.pdf); equations, which have no text layer, read on the page images. Printed page = PDF page − 11

bibliography.corrections: it is a Master of Arts thesis (Department of Geography / Centre for Earth Observation Science), not an MSc: Cooley, P. M. 1997. Mapping the nearshore substrates and hydrodynamics in lakes. MA thesis, University of Manitoba, Winnipeg (August 1997). http://hdl.handle.net/1993/832

claims.claim: A relation cited from Rowan, h ≈ 1.66·√F (h in m; F, the maximum fetch, in km) … That relation was seen only via a search summary of a DFO report
claims.source_value: Cooley prints the relation himself as his eq. 5, h > 1.660·F^0.5 (h in m, F maximum fetch in km), derived from Rowan et al.'s (1992) deep-water criterion h > L/4 with L = 20H and H_max = 0.332·F^0.5 (Wetzel 1983)
claims.location: pp. 19–20 (PDF pp. 30–31), section 6.3.3, eqs. 1–5; p. 84 (PDF p. 95), eq. 5 applied to Lake 226
claims.conditions: the limit of Airy deep-water wave theory, read as the depth to the wave base under maximal waves
claims.note: the relation is in the full text of this thesis, so the paper's caveat that it 'was seen only via a search summary' can go; cite 'Rowan et al. 1992, as derived in Cooley 1997, eq. 5'

claims.claim: (h ≈ 1.66·√F) reproduces the 1.68-m maximum wave base reported for Experimental Lakes Area Lake 226 (Cooley 1997) … the check against Lake 226 is the project's
claims.source_value: the 1.68 m is Cooley's own model output: he mapped maximum fetch over Lake 226 (360 axes) and converted it to wave-base depth with that same eq. 5, so agreement with the relation is circular, not an independent check; the observed counterpart was the mud deposition boundary, which lay at or below the predicted boundary
claims.quote: maximum depth to the wave base for Lake 226 was estimated to be 1.68
claims.conditions: Lake 226, ELA, northwest Ontario; two substrate surveys at water levels about 2 m apart; predicted mud energy boundary and observed mud deposition boundary nearly coincide where slopes are < 10°, while gravity carries mud deeper on steeper slopes
claims.note: Cooley's own test was against the observed mud deposition boundary, and it supported the maximal-wave model in this small lake ('maximal wave conditions are the formative conditions on Lake 226', p. 136)

claims.claim: Cooley mapped 15.9 km of shore in six Experimental Lakes Area lakes
claims.quote: with a total shore length of 15.9 km
claims.conditions: Lakes 164, 165, 226, 373, 377 and 442 (each ≤ 3 km of shore); 27 ha of nearshore area; mapped to 3 m depth or 30 m offshore, Lake 226 to 7 m in two surveys (and its basin to 16 m)

claims.claim: Boulder and cobble lined several kilometers of shore but covered only about 11 % of the nearshore area to 3 m depth
claims.quote: covered several kilometers of shoreline combined, had only about 11%
claims.conditions: the tri-typic boulder–cobble class 61/52/51, found in all six lakes; small share because boulder–cobble shores are moderately to highly sloped and form narrow nearshore margins; the nearshore area ends at 3 m or 30 m offshore

claims.quote: about 40% of the area surveyed were
claims.conditions: continues on the next page: 'bi-typic detritus/sand mixtures'; pure detritus covered more than 10 %, pure bedrock and pure sand about 5 % each

claims.claim: Mixed substrate rarely extended below 2 m, 'below the wave base in most areas' (Cooley 1997)
claims.quote: because the 2m depth is below the wave base in most areas of these lakes
claims.conditions: said of the number of substrate classes falling at 2 m; 'the gradational classes in these lakes rarely exceed 2m depth'
claims.note: Cooley's term is 'gradational' classes (wave-sorted material gradients, e.g. a boulder–cobble berm grading to a sand platform), which the paper renders as 'mixed substrate'; 'gradational (wave-sorted) substrate' would be closer

claims.claim: Critical (annual-storm) waves were taken as 77 % of the maximum, after Rowan via Cooley
claims.quote: determined the critical wave height to be approximately 77% of the
claims.conditions: 77 % of the maximum wave HEIGHT, determined by Rowan et al. (1992) from observed sediment distributions; 'controlled not by the large magnitude (infrequent) storm events, but by the less intense storms which occur several times each year'
claims.note: 'several times a year' rather than 'annual'. Cooley's own Lake 226 result points the other way for a small Shield lake (maximal waves fitted), so the project's choice of 77 % for Hot Brook's 2-km fetches is an assumption worth stating; with L = 20H, 77 % of H gives 77 % of the wave-base depth

notes: The six ELA lakes are small Precambrian Shield lakes; three substrate classes (detritus, boulder/cobble, bedrock) were common to all six and covered 25 % of the combined nearshore area; 20 of 221 possible substrate combinations covered more than 80 % of it (abstract, PDF p. 6). Substrate diversity fell with depth; composition was homogeneous only on low (≤ 6°) or high (> 40°) slopes. Lake 164 was 63 % detritus, sand and their mixtures with 12 % boulder–cobble; Lake 165 nearly 80 % sand/detritus with 8 % boulder–cobble (pp. 91–94).
